prereg.rule: Among audited candidates, pick the highest robust floor = min(dev score, dev score at 10 bps cost, dev score at 150 bps borrow, lowest single-parameter perturbation score). Chosen before any candidate or baseline was run on 2021+ prices.

floors.twin-band: ineligible (earlier unaudited version, kept for comparison)

strategies.name: Ensemble vol-parity pairs
strategies.description: Three classic pairs-trading signals vote on each pair of look-alike stocks, and the average vote sets how much to bet that the pair snaps back together. Calmer pairs get more money so each pair carries similar risk, and positions are only adjusted when the target moves meaningfully.

strategies.name: Learned reversion (ridge)
strategies.description: Each year a small regularized regression learns, from the past three years only, how far a stretched price ratio between two same-sector stocks tends to snap back over the following month. The strategy bets on the pairs where the predicted snap-back comfortably beats trading costs, betting more when the prediction is stronger.

strategies.name: OU half-life pairs
strategies.description: Trades pairs of same-sector stocks whose price gap has reliably snapped back within weeks, checked separately in each of the last three years. It bets on the gap closing when it stretches unusually wide, and gives up on a trade if it takes much longer than the pair's usual recovery time.

strategies.name: Regime-guard pairs
strategies.description: Trades look-alike stocks in the same sector that have moved together for years, betting that a sudden gap between them closes. When stocks inside each sector start scattering more than usual (a turbulent regime), new bets are made smaller. Per-pair stop-losses and ban lists were tested and dropped because they cut profits more than losses.

strategies.name: Sector residual s-score
strategies.description: Each stock is compared with the average of its sector peers; when it drifts unusually far from where its peers say it should be, bet on it snapping back and hedge with the peers.

strategies.name: Smart laggard
strategies.description: Pairs of closely linked stocks from the same sector. When one twin has fallen unusually far behind the other over the past one to four weeks, buy it and short the leader, then close once the gap is back to normal. It only trades unusual gaps, ignores one-day news jumps and holds for one to two weeks, so it pays a fraction of the costs of the always-on laggard rule.

strategies.name: Twin band (unaudited v1)
strategies.description: Each stock gets a 'synthetic twin': the basket of its closest look-alike stocks that best tracks it. When a stock falls unusually far behind its twin, buy it and short the twin; when it runs ahead, do the opposite; close once the gap is back to normal.

strategies.name: Twin divergence
strategies.description: Every stock gets ten 'twins': the stocks that moved most like it over the past five years. Each week, buy the stocks that fell furthest behind their twins and short the ones that ran furthest ahead, hedging each with its twins, betting the gap closes.

strategies.name: Z-score pairs
strategies.description: Top-10 same-sector pairs by cointegration over the prior 3 years, traded with the Z-score pairs rule.

strategies.name: Z-score pairs (tuned)
strategies.description: Top-10 same-sector pairs by cointegration over the prior 3 years, traded with the Z-score pairs (tuned) rule, parameters tuned per pair on the formation window.

strategies.description: Top-10 same-sector pairs by cointegration over the prior 3 years, traded with the Kalman pairs rule.
